```{r}
GSE7904 <- getGEO(filename = "GSE7904_series_matrix.txt")
GSE9574 <- getGEO(filename = "GSE9574_series_matrix.txt")
GSE15852 <- getGEO(filename = "GSE15852_series_matrix.txt")
GSE29431 <- getGEO(filename = "GSE29431_series_matrix.txt")
GSE45827 <- getGEO(filename = "GSE45827_series_matrix.txt")
GSE54002 <- getGEO(filename = "GSE54002_series_matrix.txt")

metadata_GSE7904 <- pData(GSE7904)
metadata_GSE9574 <- pData(GSE9574)
metadata_GSE15852<- pData(GSE15852)
metadata_GSE29431 <- pData(GSE29431)
metadata_GSE45827 <- pData(GSE45827)
metadata_GSE54002 <- pData(GSE54002)



# Recode into a new 'Status' column
metadata_GSE7904 <- metadata_GSE7904 %>%
  mutate(Status = case_when(
    characteristics_ch1 == "NB" ~ "cell",
    characteristics_ch1 == "NO" ~ "control",
    TRUE ~ "tumor" # Captures Basal, BRCA1, and non-BLC
  ))


metadata_GSE9574<- metadata_GSE9574%>%
  mutate(Status = case_when(
    characteristics_ch1 == "disease-state: normal (reduction mammoplasty)" ~ "control",
    TRUE ~ "tumor"
  ))

metadata_GSE15852<- metadata_GSE15852%>%
  mutate(Status = case_when(
    source_name_ch1 == "normal breast tissue" ~ "control",
    TRUE ~ "tumor"
  ))

metadata_GSE29431 <- metadata_GSE29431 %>%
  mutate(Status = case_when(
    grepl("^Normal", title, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "control",
    TRUE ~ "tumor"
  ))


metadata_GSE45827 <- metadata_GSE45827 %>%
  mutate(Status = case_when(
    grepl("CellLine",source_name_ch1,ignore.case=TRUE) ~ "cell",
    grepl("Human Normal",source_name_ch1,ignore.case=TRUE) ~ "control",
    TRUE ~ "tumor"
  ))

metadata_GSE54002<- metadata_GSE54002%>%
  mutate(Status = case_when(
    characteristics_ch1 == "tumor/nontumor: Non-tumor" ~ "control",
    TRUE ~ "tumor"
  ))


# List of all your metadata objects
metadata_list <- list(
  GSE7904 = metadata_GSE7904,
  GSE9574 = metadata_GSE9574,
  GSE15852 = metadata_GSE15852,
  GSE29431 = metadata_GSE29431,
  GSE45827 = metadata_GSE45827,
  GSE54002 = metadata_GSE54002
)

# Filter each to keep only control and tumor, then add a Study ID
cleaned_metadata_list <- lapply(names(metadata_list), function(x) {
  metadata_list[[x]] %>%
    filter(Status %in% c("control", "tumor")) %>%
    mutate(Study = x, SampleID = rownames(.)) %>%
    select(SampleID, Status, Study)
})

# Combine into one master metadata table
master_metadata <- bind_rows(cleaned_metadata_list)
rownames(master_metadata) <- master_metadata$SampleID

table(metadata_GSE54002$Status)
```

#Filter expression matrices

```{r}

check_and_log_fixed <- function(gse_obj) {
  ex <- exprs(gse_obj)
  
  # Only transform if raw (max > 50)
  if (max(ex, na.rm = TRUE) > 50) {
    message("Log-transforming raw data with flooring...")
    
    # Floor negative values to a small positive number (e.g., 1) 
    # so that log2(1) = 0
    ex[ex <= 0] <- 1 
    exprs(gse_obj) <- log2(ex)
    
  } else {
    message("Data is already log-scaled.")
  }
  return(gse_obj)
}

# Apply the fixed function
GSE7904  <- check_and_log_fixed(GSE7904)
GSE9574  <- check_and_log_fixed(GSE9574)
GSE15852 <- check_and_log_fixed(GSE15852)
# List of expression objects
exp_list <- list(
  GSE7904 = exprs(GSE7904),
  GSE9574 = exprs(GSE9574),
  GSE15852 = exprs(GSE15852),
  GSE29431 = exprs(GSE29431),
  GSE45827 = exprs(GSE45827),
  GSE54002 = exprs(GSE54002)
)

# Filter matrices to include only the 'control' and 'tumor' samples
exp_filtered <- lapply(names(exp_list), function(x) {
  samples_to_keep <- master_metadata$SampleID[master_metadata$Study == x]
  exp_list[[x]][, samples_to_keep, drop = FALSE]
})

# Find common probes/genes across ALL datasets
common_probes<- Reduce(intersect, lapply(exp_filtered, rownames))
length(common_probes)

# Subset all matrices to these common genes and column-bind
merged_expression <- do.call(cbind, lapply(exp_filtered, function(x) x[common_probes, ]))
dim(merged_expression)


fData(GSE15852)
```
#Batch Correction
```{r}

mod <- model.matrix(~as.factor(Status), data = master_metadata)

# Run ComBat to remove the 'Study' effect
# This might take a minute depending on your RAM
final_expression_clean <- ComBat(dat = merged_expression, 
                                 batch = master_metadata$Study, 
                                 mod = mod,
                                 par.prior = TRUE) # Uses parametric empirical Bayes
```
```{r}
# 1. Transpose the matrix (PCA expects samples as rows, genes as columns)
pca_data <- t(final_expression_clean)

# 2. Run PCA (scale. = TRUE is recommended for gene expression)
pca_res <- prcomp(pca_data, scale. = TRUE)

# 3. Create a plotting dataframe
# We join the PCA coordinates with your master_metadata
pca_plot_df <- data.frame(
  SampleID = rownames(pca_res$x),
  PC1 = pca_res$x[, 1],
  PC2 = pca_res$x[, 2],
  Study = master_metadata$Study,
  Status = master_metadata$Status
)

# 4. Calculate variance explained for the axis labels
var_explained <- round(100 * pca_res$sdev^2 / sum(pca_res$sdev^2), 1)

# 5. Plot coloring by Study
ggplot(pca_plot_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Status)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "PCA of Merged Breast Cancer Datasets (Post-ComBat)",
    subtitle = "Checking for remaining Batch Effects",
    x = paste0("PC1 (", var_explained[1], "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", var_explained[2], "%)")
  ) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") # Good for distinguishing 5-6 studies


```
```{r}
library(pheatmap)
library(matrixStats)

# 1. Sort the metadata and the expression matrix by 'Status'
# This ensures all 'control' are on the left and 'tumor' on the right
ordered_indices <- order(master_metadata$Status)
metadata_sorted <- master_metadata[ordered_indices, ]
expression_sorted <- final_expression_clean[, ordered_indices]

# 2. Select the top 50 genes (as you did before)
rv <- rowVars(expression_sorted)
idx <- order(rv, decreasing = TRUE)[1:50]

# 3. Plot without column clustering
pheatmap(expression_sorted[idx, ], 
         annotation_col = metadata_sorted[, "Status", drop=FALSE],
         cluster_cols = FALSE,   # This stops the patients from being clustered
         show_colnames = FALSE, 
         main = "Top 50 Varied Genes: Grouped by Status",
         color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100),
         scale = "row")         # Highly recommended to see gene-wise changes
```



```{r}
library(randomForest)
library(caret)

# 1. Prepare Data
# Transpose expression matrix: Samples as rows, Genes as columns
X <- t(final_expression_clean)
y <- as.factor(master_metadata$Status)

# 2. Split into Training (70%) and Testing (30%)
set.seed(123) # For reproducibility
trainIndex <- createDataPartition(y, p = 0.7, list = FALSE)

X_train <- X[trainIndex, ]
y_train <- y[trainIndex]
X_test  <- X[-trainIndex, ]
y_test  <- y[-trainIndex]

# 3. Train Random Forest 
# We use 'sampsize' to handle class imbalance (undersampling the majority class)
table(y_train) # Check your counts
min_class <- min(table(y_train))

rf_model <- randomForest(
  x = X_train, 
  y = y_train, 
  ntree = 500, 
  importance = TRUE,
  sampsize = c(min_class, min_class) # Forces equal representation in each tree
)

# 4. Evaluate the Model
predictions <- predict(rf_model, X_test)
conf_matrix <- confusionMatrix(predictions, y_test)
print(conf_matrix)

# 5. Find Top Biomarkers (Important Genes)
varImpPlot(rf_model, n.var = 20, main = "Top 20 Gene Predictors for Breast Cancer")
```
